summary.oneLiner: Integrated Indian manufacturer of Acrylic Fibre and CPP (Cast Polypropylene) packaging films that has diversified into grain-based Ethanol production for blending with petrol.
summary.business: Pasupati Acrylon Limited manufactures Acrylic Fibre (used in apparel, sweaters, sportswear, home furnishing and industrial cloth) and CPP packaging films (used in food & beverage, cosmetics and healthcare packaging), serving both domestic and export markets. The Company has also commissioned a grain-based Ethanol plant that sells ethanol to Oil Marketing Companies for blending with petrol under India's EBP programme.

currentContext.strengths: Acrylic Fibre plant set up in technical collaboration with SNIA BPD Italy (FIAT group), a proven world leader in acrylic fibre manufacturing, with advanced technology, automation and computerized process control|Captive power for Acrylic Fibre operations supports efficiency and reliability|European machinery for CPP film gives a quality edge over other producers|Long-term supply contracts with suppliers in the films division mitigate raw-material price volatility
currentContext.strategies: Focus on increasing exports of Acrylic Fibre and CPP Film to mitigate currency and margin pressure from imported, crude-derived raw materials|Cost optimisation through alternate sourcing, standardization, process improvements and operational efficiency to drive savings|Long-term supply contracts with suppliers in the films division to mitigate raw-material price volatility|Diversification into grain-based Ethanol as a new growth segment, commissioned and ramped during the year|Continued investment in equipment, processes and systems to ensure full compliance with manufacturing and quality/audit norms|The Company's principal financial liabilities comprise loans/borrowings and trade and other payables to support its operations, funded principally by investments, trade and other receivables, and cash and cash equivalents from operations. Financial risk activities (market and credit risk) are governed by Board-reviewed policies, with derivative activities carried out only by specialists and a policy that no trading in derivatives for speculative purposes may be undertaken.
currentContext.expansion: The Company successfully commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based Ethanol Plant and commenced commercial production in March 2025. It subsequently filed an application to enhance the Ethanol plant's capacity from 150 KL per day to 180 KL per day to improve operational efficiency, and has received consents from the respective departments/authorities for this enhancement.
currentContext.mdna: Acrylic fibre market projected to grow at 3.5%-4.00% CAGR till 2035, driven by apparel & textile industry growth, rising disposable income and population growth|Growing usage of acrylic fibres in blends with wool, cotton, polyester etc. expected to provide a strong thrust to acrylic fibre demand|Global CPP packaging film market expected to reach US$ 8,742.2 Mn by 2033 at a 5% CAGR, driven by food & beverage packaging demand and growth in e-commerce/retail|CPP film demand supported by rising consumption of convenience foods, packaged foods and pharmaceutical packaging needs|India achieved its 20% ethanol blending target (E20) ahead of schedule; national ethanol production capacity has surged to about 2,000 crore litres annually versus current blending demand of about 1,100 crore litres, indicating a demand-supply gap and future growth potential for producers|Ethanol market opportunity seen expanding beyond transportation into aviation biofuels, bio-based chemicals, power generation and other industrial applications|India's GDP growth of 7.7% in FY2025-26, supported by robust domestic consumption and sustained investment momentum, expected to support demand growth across the Company's segments|India expected to account for a substantial share of the global acrylic fibre market given expansion of the domestic textile industry and rising yarn/fibre exports
